deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is not a Riemann manuscript page. It is the first page of a letter from Karl Hattendorff, written in Aachen and dated 9 November 1875, to a 'Hochgeehrter Herr College'. The addressee is very probably Heinrich Weber, who was then preparing Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). The letter is about the editorial note to be printed with Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung'. Hattendorff had edited that memoir from Riemann's papers and conversations, and it was published in the Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13 (1867).

Content, paraphrased:
(1) Hattendorff thanks the addressee for his letter of the 6th of the month. He also thanks him for the good reception given to Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's lectures on the potential. This edition appeared as 'Schwere, Elektricität und Magnetismus', 1876.
(2) He encloses a short introduction to the minimal-surface memoir. In his view it could end with the words 'in dieselbe Zeit fallen'. This is presumably a statement that Riemann's work and Weierstrass's 1866 Berlin Monatsberichte work on minimal surfaces date from the same time.
(3) If H. A. Schwarz is to be mentioned, Hattendorff proposes appending the end of the introduction he had already sent in manuscript, from the words 'Die von Weierstrass auf der einen, etc.' He gives his reason: he does not wish to appear to be deliberately neglecting Schwarz.
(4) The sentence 'In diesem [Falle]...' continues on the next page. There Hattendorff asks that, in that case, his friend Schondorff also be named. Schondorff's Göttingen prize essay (1868) on the minimal surface bounded by a skew quadrilateral stands to Riemann as Schwarz's prize work stands to Weierstrass.

The previous page in the bundle is the end of a different, earlier Hattendorff letter. That letter tells how the M.S. came into being in Riemann's last months and proposes a note on Weierstrass's simultaneous solution.

There are no derivations to reconstruct or fill in.

results.what: Editorial correspondence on the priority note (Riemann vs. Weierstrass, with mention of Schwarz and Schondorff) for the reprint of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir in the Gesammelte Werke
results.modern_name: Plateau problem / Weierstrass–Enneper representation of minimal surfaces (historical context only; no mathematics on the page)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous, ed. Hattendorff 1867) and Weierstrass (1866) for the general method; Schwarz (1865–67) for the skew-quadrilateral surface

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a publisher/editor letter by Hattendorff (1875) with no mathematical content. Its historical information (Riemann–Weierstrass simultaneity, Schwarz and Schondorff prize works, Hattendorff's editions) is well documented in the editorial notes of Riemann's Werke.
transcription_corrections: 'Ihn[?] im M.S.' should read 'sie im M.S.' ('wie ich sie im M.S. bereits übersandt habe'), i.e. the concluding passage of the introduction, not a person.
Last line: 'Zu diesem' should read 'In diesem' (continuing 'Falle' on the next page).
'Minimalflächen' may be singular 'Minimalfläche' in the image (the plural reading is uncertain).
This page is a letter by K. Hattendorff, not a Riemann autograph. It begins a new letter distinct from the one ending on the previous page.
